english.title: Fail to notify the transfer of a shotgun
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a party to the transfer of a shotgun, namely **(..SPECIFY..), and being the holder of a

(A)_[certificate]_
(B)_[visitor's permit]_

relating to that shotgun, failed to comply with section 33(2) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997 in that you did not, within seven days of the transfer, give notice, by registered post or recorded delivery service, to the Chief Officer of Police for **(..SPECIFY THE POLICE FORCE..) who had granted your

(C)_[certificate]_
(D)_[permit]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 33(4) and 36(b) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
party to transfer of shotgun
certificate holder
visitor's permit holder
not give seven days notice of transfer
chief officer of police
who granted certificate / permit

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: See also the associated offence wording H1272 re failure to give proper notice of transfer of shotgun.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
48 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
